perspective:
From Ethan Mohamud’s perspective, he has access to the following:

- He and Gary Guo have been close friends since middle school and have relied on each other for emotional and professional support. Ethan knows Gary is a doctor and that their career paths differ.
- Ethan noticed Gary working excessively long hours at the hospital, often skipping meals and sacrificing sleep.
- Ethan became concerned and invited Gary to a weekend retreat for relaxation and rejuvenation.
- Ethan told Gary that his health matters, that he hated seeing him like this, and asked him to go for two days because it might give him a new perspective. Gary replied that he appreciated the concern but couldn’t because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. Ethan suspected there was more to Gary’s overworking than professional obligations.
- Ethan confronted Gary, reminding him they had been friends since middle school and saying he could tell him anything and that he was there to help, not judge. Gary said it was complicated and that he didn’t want to burden Ethan.
- After that, Gary opened up to Ethan about the pressures of managing a new department and personal challenges he was facing. Ethan felt relief and empathy.
- Ethan suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating responsibilities. Gary agreed, saying he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary, discussed his progress and remaining challenges, saw Gary making efforts to change, felt hopeful and proud, and offered support and encouragement. Gary told him things were better, he was less overwhelmed, and he had time for a movie.
- After a year, Ethan saw that Gary had adjusted to a healthier work-life balance and could manage on his own. Ethan felt satisfied and happy for him, decided to step back, and told Gary he was always just a call away and that he knew Gary had this. Gary thanked him and said he couldn’t have done it without Ethan’s support and felt more in control.

Ethan does not have access to any private information about Gary that was not stated or shown in his presence.
